subject.title: chat.history leaks system-level memory injection blocks to WebChat UI

question: Should `chat.history` hide legacy free-text memory-system prompt rows by pattern, or require structured provenance/plugin-origin marking before memory prompts are hidden from user-visible history?
rationale: The source-backed gap is clear for the legacy text shape, but the permanent boundary affects security visibility and could suppress legitimate user text if solved with broad pattern matching.

options.title: Structured provenance plus narrow legacy fallback
options.body: Prefer structured hidden prompt markers for current/future memory prompts and allow only a narrowly tested legacy fallback for observed shipped transcript rows.

options.title: Text-pattern filter now
options.body: Strip the known `Memory system` and heartbeat prompt text at the history boundary, accepting the risk that lookalike user text may be hidden.

options.title: Wait for live repro
options.body: Defer code changes until a current-main WebChat run with the external memory plugin proves the legacy row is still produced.

recommendation.title: Structured provenance plus narrow legacy fallback
recommendation.body: Prefer structured hidden prompt markers for current/future memory prompts and allow only a narrowly tested legacy fallback for observed shipped transcript rows.

likelyOwner.reason: The current shared projection lines and tests are attributed to this recent merged work, so this is the best available owner for the history-boundary choice.
